answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a public escrow before it may submit bids, with rewards paid only after independent peers confirm completed work. A newcomer can still join, but creating thousands of identities no longer creates free influence: the attacker must buy and immobilize tokens for every identity, risking slashing if those agents collude or abandon jobs. The ocean of bids then reflects funded commitments, while cedar and basalt serve as memorable labels in the ledger, not substitutes for stake.
